title: Held review follow-ups: question exit-5 wording, a --fields guard, a legacy-record decode test, and sweep/test tidy-ups
description:
HELD -- filed from the #616 (QCLI-504) and #617 (QCLI-501) reviewer verdicts. Do NOT start until team-lead says so.

From #616:
(a) ports/questions.ts:20 and CHANGELOG:26 -- an ASK loser reaches exit 5 through question_id_taken with NO lock-wait expiry involved, so the wording must name BOTH causes for ask, not only the expiry.
(b) command-help.ts:19 -- split the --fields sentence in two so the refusing commands are not attached to the accepting ones, and name the `task list --across-refs` exclusion.
(c) Add a guard that derives the manifest entries whose filters include "fields", asserts the help names exactly those, and that every other command rejects --fields with exit 2.
(d) The lock-release test comment should carry a mutation-verified claim -- but only after the mutation is actually run.
(e) Add a test that a newline-less pre-existing question record still decodes.
(f) Re-measure the 15s sweep bound; the honest sample spread was 6.62-12.11s.
(g) Pre-existing: an exit-5 question write surfaces the bare message "question_store_conflict" with no sentence or hint.

From #617:
(h) Give the partition guard test (test/cli-tracker-process.test.ts:1455-1463) an explicit 15_000 timeout -- on a filtered run it can pay the cold fixture build inside the bun 5s default.
(i) Drop the vestigial expect(stdout).toBeDefined() in the payload-subset loop.
(j) The QCLI-501 notes say the task group has 16 commands; it has 14.
